ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. goes

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

4. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

5. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

7. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

9. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. run

10. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary: and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in use 5.3.1 Word Classes: Adjectives and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

2. A — went

3. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

8. D — Where is the library?

9. D — run

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

11. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary:; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in use 5.3.1 Word Classes: Adjectives; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
